issue_context.title: Using modifyCount in the optimizer can inflate estimation compared to realtimeRowCount

review_comments: I guess we can still keep this?
You are correct - will add it back
I guess it's just an arbitrary number to make the final estimated results not too aggressive.

I used 0.5 because I did not want to always assume that any new rows added, or updates to the existing rows were all changing the high end 100% or the low end 100%. If you started with 100 rows, and you added 10 rows - you could've added 5 rows outside the low bound, and 5 rows above the high bound. Or all above or below - or all within the range. Assuming all rows added are 100% in one direction cannot be verified - therefore - 0.5 is used.

Can you give an example of where this change would help? I can understand the changes, but I don't understand the impact of this change. Forgive me for asking too many questions. I just want to make sure I understand the motivation behind this change.

Simple example - if I have a table with 100 rows, and values 1 to 100.
Select count(*) from t where a > 100; <-- will return count == 0.

If I insert 10 rows, values 101 to 110 - and do NOT run ANALYZE - realtimeRowCount == 110.

Select count(*) from t where a > 100; <-- now the result is count == 10 (because I added 10 values after 100.

Now I run ANALYZE (so rowCount == 110), then insert another 10 rows - this time with values 1-10 - realtimeRowCount == 120.
select count(*) from t where a > 110; <-- realtimeRowCount == 120 - and I don't know that the 10 new rows aren't greater than 110.

`If the realtimeRowCount is larger than the original table rows, then any out of range estimate is unreliable.` Is this assumption too conservative (or strict)? As long as the data has increased since the last Analyze, this assumption will be satisfied.

I'm not sure whether `the realtimeRowCount is larger than the original table rows` is too conservative, what do you think of adding an percentage here like 20%, for example, `realtimeRowCount >= hg.TotalRowCount() * (1+20%)`? @terry1purcell

@qw4990 - you are correct that any changes which result in an increase in realtimeRowCount will cause a change from this code. However - for this code to be entered - you must be searching for values outside of the range of the current histograms. If the predicates do not search outside this range - then there is no impact from this change.

Using an example such as 20% would miss those situations where a small number of rows were added - similar to the example that I shared above.
